We visited Dr. Rajeev Nerurkar (ENT/Otorhinolaryngologist) regarding my mother’s recurring eye swelling. Although the problem was limited to one eye, he recommended operating on both eyes.

He referred us to another doctor for pre-operative fitness, as my mother is diabetic and has high blood pressure. We were advised to conduct multiple tests, including a chest X-ray, diabetes tests, blood pressure evaluation, and a 2D Echo. Despite the high costs, we completed all the tests. After reviewing the reports, both doctors confirmed that my mother was fit for surgery.

The surgery was scheduled for 12th March. We were instructed to admit my mother a day prior, on 11th March before 5 PM, and were informed that the operation would take place between 8 AM and 12 PM, specifically at 10 AM. My mother was asked to remain fasting from the previous night.

However, on the day of the surgery, even by 9:30 AM, she had not been taken to the operation theatre. Upon inquiry, the nursing staff informed us that they had not received instructions from the doctor. When I contacted Dr. Nerurkar, he initially did not respond. Later, he informed us via message that the surgery was postponed to 1:30 PM, citing that he had not received the fitness report the previous night—this delay was not communicated to us in advance.

Subsequently, during a phone call, he stated that there was no guarantee that the issue would not recur even after surgery. This was contrary to his earlier assurance that surgery was the only effective solution. When I sought clarification, he stated that he would not proceed with the surgery as I was asking too many questions. He then cancelled the procedure and discharged my mother.

Further, after this, he sent a message stating that he could suggest a plastic surgeon as he would not be able to perform the surgery. This raises serious concerns, as if he was not in a position to proceed, it should have been communicated earlier instead of subjecting us to repeated consultations, unnecessary tests, and significant financial expense.

This entire experience was highly unprofessional and distressing. We incurred considerable costs on consultations, diagnostic tests, and hospital charges (approximately ₹10,000 for the day of admission), without any resolution. Dr. Sankhe immediately started me on a nasal spray and appropriate anti-allergy medication. She also guided me on practical steps to reduce dust mite exposure at home. Within days, I noticed a significant improvement. My sneezing reduced dramatically, my nose felt clearer, and I started sleeping peacefully again. Now, I feel lighter, more energetic, and much more in control of my health.

What truly stood out to me was her compassionate approach. She didn’t just treat my symptoms — she helped me understand my condition. That clarity itself reduced half my stress.

If you are suffering from unexplained allergies, I strongly encourage you not to ignore it. Getting a proper diagnosis through a simple test can completely change your quality of life. I am genuinely grateful for the care I received and so happy with the results.

Thank you, Dr. Krupa Sankhe, for helping me breathe freely again!
